name: Veltran MedSync Post-Op Compression Suit
description: Full-body compression garment in clinical off-white with color-coded gradient banding — blue at the extremities grading to warm amber at the core — indicating zone-specific compression levels. Issued post-augmentation surgery or major geneware integration. Micro-conductive threads embedded in the fabric monitor swelling, temperature differentials, and tissue resistance, transmitting passive data to a paired BCI or clinic receiver. Seams are laser-bonded rather than stitched to prevent irritation at surgical margins. Zipper channels allow access without full removal.
functionality: Biometric monitoring of post-surgical sites via BCI or external receiver; graduated compression by body zone; zipper-access panels for wound care without removal; anti-microbial fabric for extended wear during recovery.
what_it_says: You've been rebuilt recently — and whether the procedure was elective or emergency says everything about who paid for it.

story_hooks: A Tier 2 factory worker is wearing a Veltran suit weeks after their employer's mandatory chrome-arm replacement — the biometric data it's been logging would be very interesting to a labor attorney.
The clinic that issued this suit closed suddenly; the data receiver it paired to is now broadcasting to an unknown address.
Someone is wearing this under street clothes, months past any normal recovery window — either they never healed right, or they don't want anyone to know what was done to them.
